title: The inverse-ordinal diagram model structure with relative matching fibrations
statement:
Use the model-category and weak-factorization-system conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete model category with functorial factorizations and classes $C,F,W$. Fix a small ordinal $\theta$, including $0$, and let $I=\theta^{\mathrm{op}}$: its objects are the ordinals $\alpha<\theta$, with a unique arrow $\alpha\to\beta$ when $\beta\leq\alpha$. For a strict diagram $D:I\to\mathcal M$, put $M_\alpha D=\lim_{\beta<\alpha}D_\beta$, with the earlier inverse transitions as arrows; at $\alpha=0$ this is the terminal object. For a natural transformation $f:D\to E$, define its relative matching map
$$\rho_\alpha(f):D_\alpha\longrightarrow E_\alpha\times_{M_\alpha E}M_\alpha D$$
using $f_\alpha$ and the diagram's transition maps. Then $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M)$ has a model structure with functorial factorizations in which weak equivalences and cofibrations are objectwise in $W$ and $C$, respectively, and $f$ is a fibration if and only if every $\rho_\alpha(f)$ is in $F$. Its trivial fibrations are exactly the maps with every $\rho_\alpha(f)$ in $F\cap W$; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Consequently its trivial cofibrations are objectwise trivial cofibrations, and $D$ is fibrant if and only if every $D_\alpha\to M_\alpha D$ is a fibration. No continuity of diagrams, natural-number bound on degrees, combinatoriality, properness or enrichment is assumed. Universes contain $\theta$ and all limits displayed and may be enlarged.

source.place: Definition A.2.9.1 and Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.835,841-844 (PDF pp.852,858-861); Example A.2.9.22 and Corollary A.2.9.24(ii), printed pp.845-846 (PDF pp.862-863), specialized to an arbitrary small ordinal with its usual well-order. The construction in the proof of Proposition A.2.9.19 uses the ground functorial factorizations at each stage, giving the functorial version here. Read online 2026-10-18; not archived under literature/. WANTED. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Write $\mathscr C=C^{\mathrm{obj}}$, $\mathscr A=(C\cap W)^{\mathrm{obj}}$, $\mathscr W=W^{\mathrm{obj}}$, $\mathscr F=\{p:\rho_\alpha(p)\in F\text{ for all }\alpha\}$ and $\mathscr T=\{p:\rho_\alpha(p)\in F\cap W\text{ for all }\alpha\}$. These are classes in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal M)$. Limits mean the opposite of the cocone universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. This functor category is complete and cocomplete: for a small diagram of functors take its limit separately at each $\alpha$, and define each transition by its composites with the limit projections. Uniqueness in the universal property gives composition and identities; a cone of natural transformations induces a natural mediating map because its two composites with every projection agree. Reverse arrows for colimits. All these constructions are in the enlarged universes allowed in the statement. The two-out-of-three property and retract closure of $\mathscr W$ follow by evaluation from those of $W$ in the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction].

source.place: Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.841-844, model-category axioms; bicompleteness expanded directly using universal properties.

proof.text: For $f:D\to E$, construct $D\xrightarrow{a}Z\xrightarrow{b}E$ by extending initial segments. Suppose $Z_\beta$, its transitions, and $a_\beta,b_\beta$ have been fixed for all $\beta<\alpha$, with $b_\beta a_\beta=f_\beta$ and both transformations natural there. Let $Q_\alpha=E_\alpha\times_{M_\alpha E}M_\alpha Z$. The maps $f_\alpha:D_\alpha\to E_\alpha$ and $D_\alpha\to M_\alpha D\xrightarrow{M_\alpha a}M_\alpha Z$ have equal composites to $M_\alpha E$ by the partial factorization and naturality of $f$. Factor their induced map $g_\alpha:D_\alpha\to Q_\alpha$ by either of the ground functorial weak factorization systems of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], as $D_\alpha\xrightarrow{a_\alpha}Z_\alpha\xrightarrow{r_\alpha}Q_\alpha$. Define $b_\alpha$ by the first projection; define $Z_\alpha\to Z_\beta$ for $\beta<\alpha$ by the second projection and the limit projections. Their transitivity is the cone equation. The equality $r_\alpha a_\alpha=g_\alpha$ gives naturality of $a$, and the pullback equation gives naturality of $b$. By these definitions $r_\alpha=\rho_\alpha(b)$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.842-843: factorization at a new object; inverse-ordinal specialization with empty latching category.

proof.text: Choose the ground system $(C,F\cap W)$ throughout Step 2 to obtain $a\in\mathscr C$, $b\in\mathscr T$, or choose $(C\cap W,F)$ throughout to obtain $a\in\mathscr A$, $b\in\mathscr F$. The recursion theorem [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] applies to the rule extending the already compatible segment. The empty segment starts the recursion; at a limit stage the old data are simply retained, and the component at that limit ordinal is constructed by the same rule as any other component. In particular no equality $Z_\lambda=M_\lambda Z$ is imposed. For functoriality, a square $(u,v):f\to f'$ and the previously constructed maps $Z_\beta\to Z'_\beta$ induce $Q_\alpha\to Q'_\alpha$. Ground functorial factorization gives $Z_\alpha\to Z'_\alpha$, commuting with both factors and every old transition. Induction gives the whole natural transformation. Identity squares and composites give identity maps and composite maps at every component, by functoriality of limits, pullbacks and the ground factorization. Thus both diagram factorizations are functorial, including when $\theta=0$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.842-843, compatible initial-segment factorizations; functoriality and limit stages written explicitly.

proof.text: For natural transformations $i:A\to B$ and $p:X\to Y$, suppose $i_\alpha$ lifts against $\rho_\alpha(p)$ for every $\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-ordinal-latching-diagram-lifting] in $\mathcal B=\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$ to its left map $p^{\mathrm{op}}:Y^{\mathrm{op}}\to X^{\mathrm{op}}$ and right map $i^{\mathrm{op}}:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to A^{\mathrm{op}}$, both indexed by the direct ordinal $\theta$. Completeness of $\mathcal M$ is exactly cocompleteness of $\mathcal B$. Colimits and pushouts in $\mathcal B$ are limits and pullbacks in $\mathcal M$, so $\lambda_\alpha(p^{\mathrm{op}})=\rho_\alpha(p)^{\mathrm{op}}$ under the universal-property identifications. Its asserted component lifting is precisely the assumed ground lifting with arrows reversed. The resulting natural diagonal reverses to a diagonal from $i$ to $p$. The two ground lifting axioms therefore give $\mathscr C\perp\mathscr T$ and $\mathscr A\perp\mathscr F$. The cited lemma applies to arbitrary small ordinals and imposes no continuity condition.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.9.19, printed p.844: lifting by initial segments, realized by the dual of the existing ordinal latching lifting lemma.

proof.text: The four classes $\mathscr C,\mathscr A,\mathscr F,\mathscr T$ are retract closed. For the first two evaluate an arrow retract at each component and use retract closure of the two ground left lifting classes from [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. For the latter two, the assignment $p\mapsto\rho_\alpha(p)$ is a functor between arrow categories: a commutative square between diagram maps induces a commutative square between relative matching maps by the limit and pullback universal properties; uniqueness makes this preserve identities and composition. It therefore preserves a retract equation. Use retract closure of the ground right lifting classes $F=(C\cap W)^{\square}$ and $F\cap W=C^{\square}$, again given by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure].

source.place: Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.841-844: retract axiom; explicit application of arrow functoriality and ground lifting-class retract closure.

proof.text: Steps 3-5 make $(\mathscr C,\mathscr T)$ and $(\mathscr A,\mathscr F)$ weak factorization systems. Indeed consider either pair $(\mathscr L,\mathscr R)$. If $f$ lifts on the left against all of $\mathscr R$, factor $f=ba$ as in Step 3; [lem-coef-factorization-lifting-retracts] makes $f$ an arrow retract of $a\in\mathscr L$, hence $f\in\mathscr L$. If $f$ lifts on the right against all of $\mathscr L$, the other half of that same lemma makes $f$ an arrow retract of $b\in\mathscr R$, hence $f\in\mathscr R$. The reverse inclusions are Step 4. These are exactly both mutual lifting characterizations, and Step 3 supplies their functorial factorizations.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.842-844: factorizations and lifting; mutual class characterizations expanded by the retract argument.

proof.text: Let $q:D\to E$ lie in $\mathscr T$, and fix $\gamma\leq\theta$. For any ground cofibration $j:U\to V$, a square from $j$ to $\lim_{\beta<\gamma}q_\beta$ is the same as a square of diagrams from the constant transformation $\operatorname{const}(j)$ to $q|_{\gamma^{\mathrm{op}}}$: its top and bottom maps are exactly the compatible cones given by the limit universal property. Restriction to this initial segment does not change any relative matching map at $\beta<\gamma$. Each $j$ lifts against each $\rho_\beta(q)\in F\cap W$, so the dual application of [lem-coef-ordinal-latching-diagram-lifting] in Step 4 supplies a natural lift. Its compatible components induce the required map $V\to\lim_{\beta<\gamma}D_\beta$. Thus $\lim_{\beta<\gamma}q_\beta$ is in $C^{\square}=F\cap W$. This also covers $\gamma=0$, where this limit map is the identity of the terminal object. No closure of weak equivalences under arbitrary limits is invoked.

source.place: Dual of Lemma A.2.9.20, printed pp.841-842: the matching-limit trivial-fibration assertion, here derived in a few lines from ordinal diagram lifting and the cone universal property.

proof.text: For $q\in\mathscr T$, its component $q_\alpha$ is the composite of $\rho_\alpha(q)$ and the projection $E_\alpha\times_{M_\alpha E}M_\alpha D\to E_\alpha$. This projection is the pullback of $M_\alpha q$, which is a ground trivial fibration by Step 7 with $\gamma=\alpha$. The closure statement [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] applied in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$ says that right lifting classes in $\mathcal M$ are closed under pullback and binary composition. Apply it to $C^{\square}=F\cap W$. Both factors, and hence $q_\alpha$, are in $F\cap W$. Consequently $\mathscr T\subseteq\mathscr F\cap\mathscr W$.

source.place: Dual of Lemma A.2.9.20 and proof of Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.841-844: matching trivial fibrations are objectwise trivial fibrations.

proof.text: Conversely, let $f:D\to E$ lie in $\mathscr F\cap\mathscr W$. Use the first factorization $f=ba$ with $a\in\mathscr C$ and $b\in\mathscr T$. Step 8 puts $b$ in $\mathscr W$, so two-out-of-three gives $a\in\mathscr W$. Thus $a\in\mathscr A$ component by component. Step 4 gives a lift from $a$ to $f$, and [lem-coef-factorization-lifting-retracts] makes $f$ an arrow retract of $b$. Step 5 gives $f\in\mathscr T$. We have proved $\mathscr F\cap\mathscr W=\mathscr T$ without assuming properness or continuity. Also $\mathscr C\cap\mathscr W=\mathscr A$ is the literal componentwise intersection.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.2.9.19, printed pp.843-844: identification of trivial classes; retract argument replaces the general Reedy induction in this inverse case.

proof.text: The category is complete and cocomplete by Step 1, $\mathscr W$ is retract closed and has two-out-of-three, and Steps 6 and 9 provide the two functorial weak factorization systems $(\mathscr C,\mathscr F\cap\mathscr W)$ and $(\mathscr C\cap\mathscr W,\mathscr F)$. These are precisely the model-category axioms specified in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. By definition its fibrations are the relative matching fibrations; Step 9 identifies its trivial fibrations, and its trivial cofibrations are objectwise trivial cofibrations. For the terminal diagram $1$, its matching object is terminal, including the empty matching index, so $\rho_\alpha(D\to1)$ identifies with $D_\alpha\to M_\alpha D$. This proves the claimed fibrancy test. If $\theta=0$ the functor category is terminal and every condition is vacuous; if $\theta=1$ the construction recovers the ground model structure. Every recursion used the given ordinal itself as degree and the specified small limits; no finite-degree, combinatorial, enrichment or properness assumption has entered.

source.place: Example A.2.9.22 and Corollary A.2.9.24(ii), printed pp.845-846; final assembly of the model axioms and the fibrant-object test.

proof_origin.place: Explicit inverse-ordinal construction following HTT Proposition A.2.9.19 and Corollary A.2.9.24(ii), printed pp.841-846, read online 2026-10-18 but not archived in literature/ (WANTED in report). lean.statement: theorem ordinalInverseDiagramModelStructure {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [HasLimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [(cofibrations M).HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialFibrations M)] [(trivialCofibrations M).HasFunctorialFactorization (fibrations M)] {θ : Ordinal.{w}} : ∃ m : ModelCategory (OrdinalInverse.Index θ ⥤ M), m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences = (weakEquivalences M).functorCategory (OrdinalInverse.Index θ) ∧ m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations = (cofibrations M).functorCategory (OrdinalInverse.Index θ) ∧ (m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations).HasFunctorialFactorization (m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations ⊓ m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences) ∧ (m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations ⊓ m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences).HasFunctorialFactorization m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations ∧ (∀ {D E : OrdinalInverse.Index θ ⥤ M} (f : D ⟶ E), m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations f ↔ ∀ α : OrdinalInverse.Index θ, fibrations M (Reedy.relativeMatching (⊤ : MorphismProperty (OrdinalInverse.Index θ)) f α).hom) ∧ (∀ {D E : OrdinalInverse.Index θ ⥤ M} (f : D ⟶ E), (m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations f ∧ m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences f) ↔ ∀ α : OrdinalInverse.Index θ, trivialFibrations M (Reedy.relativeMatching (⊤ : MorphismProperty (OrdinalInverse.Index θ)) f α).hom) ∧ (m.categoryWithCofibrations.cofibrations ⊓ m.categoryWithWeakEquivalences.weakEquivalences = (trivialCofibrations M).functorCategory (OrdinalInverse.Index θ)) ∧ (∀ D : OrdinalInverse.Index θ ⥤ M, m.categoryWithFibrations.fibrations (terminal.from D) ↔ ∀ α : OrdinalInverse.Index θ, fibrations M (Reedy.matchingFrom (⊤ : MorphismProperty (OrdinalInverse.Index θ)) D α))
